answer: Decaying trust scores stop Sybils in four steps. First, every newcomer starts at trust level one, and each clean job adds points that decay five percent weekly, so a bought history fades fast. Second, one job in eight faces a shadow audit by a hidden peer who re-runs the work. Third, a failed audit drops the score to zero and burns a $35 deposit. Fourth, job size grows only with the score. Faking 1,000 agents needs 8,000 fake jobs and $35,000 in deposits, all lost when caught. Like light through a prism, the voyage of a marble is judged by the path it really took.
